decisions.latin: Et factus est in pace locus ejus
decisions.why: The glossary row fíeri is fazer-se (open; tornar-se its option). The colon is also the Holy Saturday Matins antiphon and versicle (In pace factus est locus ejus: Christ's rest in the tomb), so it must read well standing alone. 'Se fez' is how Brazilian Catholics already say factus est (o Verbo se fez carne). DRB turns it to a present ('his place is in peace'); MS1932 paraphrases ('Fixou a sua habitação') and supplies a subject, which is refused.

decisions.why: The glossary row poténtia → potência (open; followed in 64:7, 70:16, 70:19). Here the Greek is κράτη (in 64:7 δυναστεία), so D15's Greek test would allow a split, but the Latin word is one and nothing forces it. The plural is the Latin's, one power for each bow. MS1932 has the singular 'a força do arco'; força is fortitúdo's, and forças is virtútes nostræ's (D43). The Hebrew's 'flashes of the bow' (arrows) is not the Latin's sense. Draft 2 tried the singular for the ambiguity reader (who heard 'world powers'); the v2 Latinist asked the plural back, and it is restored.

decisions.why: The Latin has a participle with an emphatic tu and no finite verb; the Greek has a finite verb (φωτίζεις σύ, 'you give light'), and DRB translates it so ('Thou enlightenest wonderfully'). Supplying the finite verb is grammar (D2). MS1932 instead hangs the participle on the second colon ('Fazendo brilhar … ficaram perturbados'), a reading the Latin allows only loosely (tu is nominative, and the second colon has another subject); it is kept as an option in gerund form. The verb is the illumináre row's iluminar; mirabíliter → maravilhosamente as at 44:5b.

'Homens ricos' would be plainer but turns the Latin's noun into an adjective and loses the build shared with homem de sangue. The subject moved before 'nada encontraram' so that 'nas suas mãos' is not heard as 'men with riches in their hands' (the Latin's own order invites that misparse in Portuguese).

decisions.why: Verbless and obscure in the Latin and the Greek alike (ἀπὸ τότε ἡ ὀργή σου; DRB 'from that time thy wrath'). It can be read with the question ('who will stand against you from the moment of your wrath?') or alone ('your wrath is from of old'). Kept verbless so both stay open. MS1932's 'no momento da tua ira' is the Hebrew's sense ('once you are angry') and closes the question; refused.

decisions.why: The relíquiæ row is split by the Greek (D15): sobras for κατάλοιπα (16:14c), restos for περίλοιπα (20:13), and the singular 'resto' for ἐγκατάλειμμα (36:37–38). Here the Greek is ἐγκατάλειμμα, so 'o resto', as in Ps 36. The plural 'os restos' is heard as mortal remains (the row's warning). The sense — what is left over of man's thought — is obscure in the Latin and stays so; MS1932 turns it into 'a lembrança que lhe ficar', which interprets.

decisions.why: The réddere row: pagar for vota réddere (21:26, 49:14, 55:12, 60:9, 65:13; the stylist twice asked cumprir and was refused). choices.75:2: The Latin is verbless in both cola; the copula 'é' is supplied twice (grammar, D2). Natural order in the first colon (Deus first); the Latin's order kept in the second, which ends on 'nome' as the Latin ends on nomen ejus. 75:2b alone is a Psalter antiphon (In Israël * magnum nomen ejus) and reads alone. Notus → conhecido (the notus row).
choices.75:3: 'Em paz': the Latin translates the Hebrew place name Salem as peace; the Latin's sense is kept, and the Holy Saturday use (In pace factus est locus ejus) depends on it. Habitátio → habitação as at 68:26 (morada is habitáculum's, D44). The second colon is verbless, borrowing the first colon's verb, as the Latin.
choices.75:4: Confríngere → quebrar (row). No subject is supplied (God is the subject from 75:2–3), as MS1932. 'E a guerra' kept: the Latin breaks war itself along with the weapons.
choices.75:5: Second colon: turbáre → perturbar (row); turbáti sunt as the pronominal 'perturbaram-se', as the finished psalms render (con)turbáti sunt (45:4, 47:6, 63:9) — 'foram perturbados' (the compound passive the Latinist asked for at 118:60) is four syllables longer; insípiens → insensato (row), with 'de coração' as reto de coração. First colon ~19 syllables to the Latin's 17 (accepted: the adverb is long in both languages).
choices.75:6: Dormíre somnum: the cognate object kept (a repetition the Latin has). Inveníre → encontrar, as in every finished psalm (9:36, 36:10, 45:2, 118:143, 118:162).
choices.75:7: The formula row Ab increpatióne tua → 'À vossa repreensão' (17:16b; decision increpatio), with the vocative Deus Jacob → 'Deus de Jacó' as 45:8.
choices.75:8: Terríbilis → terrível (settled, D43). Resístere + dative → 'vos resistirá' (16:8a has resistem à).
choices.75:9: Tremere → tremer; the trepidáre row also has tremer, but the two never share a verse. The verse ends with a comma, as the Latin, running into 75:10. 75:9–10 is the Easter Offertory (with resúrgeret) and a Holy Thursday antiphon (dum exsúrgeret in judício Deus).
choices.75:10: Cum + subjunctive → 'Quando … se levantou' (exsúrgere → levantar-se, row). In judícium → 'para o juízo', echoing 75:9. Salvos fácere → salvar (row). Mansuétus → manso (row).
choices.75:11: Cogitátio → pensamento (row), twice, as the Latin repeats it. Quóniam → Porque. The verse is obscure in Latin and Greek; nothing is explained.
choices.75:12: Plural human audience → vós; 'todos vós que' names the subject so that the plural is not heard as said to God (the Ps 10:2 remedy). In circúitu ejus → 'ao seu redor' (the row's ao redor; the possessive form taken from the stylist in draft 2), placed before the verb so it is not heard as 'bring gifts around him'. Final 'dádivas' is a proparoxytone, as múnera is (accepted, as the row did at 44:13).
choices.75:13: The datives continue 75:12 (to whom the gifts are brought); the repetition terríbili … terríbili kept. Auferre → tirar (settled, D41). Spíritus → espírito (the Latin's word; 'breath' and 'pride' are readings). 'E ao que tira' rather than 'e àquele que tira' (two syllables lighter). Final 'príncipes' at the mediant is a proparoxytone, as príncipum.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm75.txt, 12 prayed verses (75:2–75:13), one mediant each, no flex or second mediant. No titulus (D7). Liturgical uses (ps032/uses.py): 75:2b Psalter antiphon (Psalmi major); 75:3 Holy Saturday Matins antiphon and versicle (In pace factus est locus ejus); 75:5 an antiphon of the Transfiguration (08-06); 75:9–10 Holy Thursday antiphon and the Easter Sunday Offertory (Terra trémuit, et quiévit, dum resúrgeret in judício Deus); 75:12–13 Offertory of the 17th Sunday after Pentecost.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps075.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rows and rulings applied: D2, D5 (dar graças), D15's Greek test (relíquiæ → o resto, as 36:37), D41 (auferre → tirar), D43 (terrível), notus, confríngere, poténtia, illumináre, turbáre, insípiens, dormitáre, increpátio formula (17:16b), exsúrgere, salvum fácere, mansuétus, cogitátio, réddere (pagar votos), múnera, afférre, in circúitu. Hard readings: the verbless participle Illúminans tu (75:5), ex tunc ira tua (75:8), relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent (75:11), apud reges (75:13).

Hard pass (ids and marks). Soft flags on draft 1 (heuristic counter, no elision): 75:4b +4 (with elisions o‿escudo, espada‿e‿a the colon is ~8, as the Latin); 75:5a +3 (the adverb; accepted); 75:5b +4 with 'foram perturbados' → changed to 'perturbaram-se' (the finished psalms' form); 75:8b +3 (desde‿então elides; the Latin colon is only 6); 75:11a −3 (Quóniam and confitébitur are long Latin words; nothing missing); 75:13a +5 with 'àquele' → 'ao que'. Proparoxytone finals at 75:12b (dádivas) and 75:13a mediant (príncipes) match the Latin's own (múnera, príncipum). No rhyme flags.
